messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High severity: GPU OOMs on prefill causing container restarts in cluster us-west1-gpupool-3. Affected service: runtime-prefill-service. Pager: @oncall-ops

oncall-ops: got it, joining bridge now — pinging SRE

sre-amy: joining, what's the scale? any cust impact?

oncall-ops: seeing ~30 container restarts across 6 nodes in last 5m; rate spikes at 12:34 UTC. preliminary metrics: 5xx spike to 2.3% from 0.1%; error sig: cuda out of memory during prefill loop.

ml-runtime-jay: logs show repeated:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 32.00 GiB total capacity; 29.50 GiB already allocated; 300.00 MiB free; 2.00 GiB reserved)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/prefill.py", line 412, in handle_prefill
    kv_cache.prefetch(tokens)
  File "/app/runtime/kv_cache.py", line 198, in prefetch
    cuda_ctx.allocate(size)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
```

ml-runtime-jay: container logs also show SIGKILL from oom-killer soon after, then k8s restarts policy triggers.

eng-runtime-sam: probable trigger: unusually long user prompts with deep context + aggressive prefetch batch size. We've seen this pattern before. Suggest immediate mitigations: reduce prefetch window and cap prefill tokens per request.

eng-runtime-sam: pushing a config hotpatch: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192 -> 2048 and PREFETCH_BATCH=8 -> 4 via configmap. rolling restart for runtime-prefill-service can be done safely.

oncall-ops: applying config change now, will monitor. @ml-runtime-jay can you add a short-lived circuit breaker to reject requests with prefill tokens > 8k and return 413? We need to protect pool.

ml-runtime-jay: yes, adding a warn+reject path. Pushing PR -> will hot-deploy to canary then rollout. ETA ~12m.

support-lucy: support is seeing ~7 customer tickets re: streaming disconnects and 5xxs. Noticing one large customer (acme-health) submitted contiguous long transcripts; flagged for potential impact.

product-ops-maria: prioritize notifying acme-health with status update: we'll do a brief note that we're mitigating root cause and may be throttling long-context requests.

oncall-ops: can we route acme-health to dedicated pool while we stabilize? any capacity?

eng-runtime-sam: maybe, but dedicated pools limited. short term we can route them to fallback model (smaller context) with explicit consent. config: routing rule add: customer:acme-health -> model:small-context-v1, fallback: cold-model.

sre-amy: monitoring: memory allocation tail has spikes correlated with requests with prefill length > 60k tokens. We'll add a metric and alert for prefills > 8k tokens hitting GPU memory > 28Gi.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://bridge.company/incident/2866666000

ml-runtime-jay: hotpatch PR merged to canary, no restarts on canary in 3m. Deploying to 30% -> 100% now.

oncall-ops: change applied, rolling restarts finishing. restarting containers are dropping to 0 after patch.

support-lucy: opening customer comms: drafting message for acme-health, staging in #support-drafts.

product-ops-maria: thanks. mark as P1 and start post-incident doc.

sre-amy: handing off to night oncall @oncall-ops-night for follow-up and RCA. leaving notes in the bridge and runbook.

oncall-ops-night: acknowledged, taking over. please paste any remaining logs or checks.

ml-runtime-jay: added prefills-per-request histogram and recent offending request ids to the bridge notes. key IDs: req-7f3a, req-9a8b, req-cc12.

oncall-ops-night: copied. putting incident in monitoring state; will update if we see regressions. closing live mitigation thread here.

support-lucy: scheduled customer updates: initial notice sent to acme-health, we'll follow-up with postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:
